question: Are GT23 RawData Joint_Moments.csv values N*m (README) or already mass-normalized N*m/kg?
selection: numpy default_rng(seed).permutation over the 12 subjects in the publisher mass table; first N_SUBJECTS; one task each by rng.integers over sorted normal/incline/weighted walking base tasks; redraw if neither side has 5 stances.

readme.line_32: Joint_Moments.csv: Joint torques from opensim (Nm) at 200 Hz.

method.lever_arm: internal ankle estimate (N*m, dorsiflexion +) = -[(cop_ap - a_x) F_vertical + a_y F_shear_ap] from Virtual_Insoles (calcn frame), (a_x, a_y) = (0.04877, 0.04195) m generic gait2392; grid [(0.02, 0.0), (0.02, 0.04), (0.02, 0.08), (0.05, 0.0), (0.05, 0.04), (0.05, 0.08), (0.08, 0.0), (0.08, 0.04), (0.08, 0.08)]; shear sign also flipped. Ignores foot weight and inertia.
method.window: (0.4, 0.9) of stance; stance = insole vertical force > 100.0 N, 0.25-2.5 s, not at a file edge, finite moment and CoP.
method.slope: least squares through the origin of the source ankle column on the N*m estimate; implied mass = 1/slope.
method.force_plate_mass: 2 x mean single-leg vertical plate force over each heel-strike-to-heel-strike period / g; median over strides.
method.power: Joint_Powers ankle vs source ankle moment x Joint_Velocities ankle in rad/s.

chips: source divides by a body mass in 8 of 8 legs: 64-90 kg, never 1 kg
plate-derived body mass matches the README mass in 5 of 5 subjects
power = moment × speed (ratio 0.96-1.00): powers are W/kg, not W
insole force = plate force (max difference 6e-12 N)
which mass the authors divided by: implied/README 0.73-1.33
hip and knee columns: same file, not lever-armed
AB03: plates give 114 kg (README 113.5, model table 82.2); source implies 86 kg

verdict.answer: RawData Joint_Moments.csv is already mass-normalized (N*m/kg), contrary to README line 32 ("Nm"). Joint_Powers.csv equals moment x angular velocity (rad/s), so it is W/kg, contrary to the README "W".
verdict.evidence: Against a mass-free force-plate lever-arm ankle moment in N*m, the source column scales by 1/(64-90 kg) in every leg (over a 3 x 3 ankle-position grid 46-113 kg); a N*m column would scale by 1. Correlation 0.997-0.9998.
verdict.prior_audit: gt23-publisher-units-and-mass-review.json accepted N*m from the README alone and proposed dividing by participant mass; that correction would double-normalize and is withdrawn. Its retraction of the earlier "already mass-normalized" claim is itself reversed by this evidence. Its AB03 mass finding stands: force plates give about 114 kg (README 113.5), not the local model table 82.18.
verdict.converters: The current converters copy raw values and label them Nm_kg; on units that is correct. Mass-dependent fields (body-weight GRF normalization) still need the publisher mass table, per the prior review.
verdict.not_resolved: Which mass the authors divided by (participant vs model mass, notably AB03 113.5 vs 82.18 kg): the generic ankle position limits the implied mass to about +/-30 %.

limitations: Ankle columns only are lever-armed; hip and knee share the file and show per-kg magnitudes (p1/p99 within about +/-2.1) but were not independently tested.
Generic gait2392 ankle position in calcn (subject models not parsed); implied mass varies 46-113 kg over the grid, so units are decided but the exact denominator is not.
Walking tasks only (incline and weighted walking drawn); 5 subjects, 8 legs.
Quasi-static lever arm ignores foot weight and inertia.
The README copy is the publisher bitstream bound by the prior review; the publisher README itself is not edited.
